source.title: Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks
source.authors: G. McCracken; Gabriela Moisescu-Pareja; Vincent Létourneau; D. Precup; J. Love

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It examines whether networks trained on modular addition share learned structure, but uses neuron fits and an abstract-algorithm analysis rather than pairwise representation-distance measures.
record.gate_note: The study tests convergence at an abstract algorithmic level on modular addition, not pairwise representational similarity. It does not test vision-language alignment or convergence as model scale and capability increase. Prior-work results mentioned in the text are not extracted as findings of this study. Frequency-count and modulus-scaling results are not rows because they do not measure alignment between models.
record.test_reason: The study tests universality across seeds, hyperparameters and architectures (MLPs, clock and pizza transformers) on modular addition. It uses neuron-level sinusoidal fits, fit-replacement ablations and frequency analyses rather than pairwise similarity metrics. Its own results bear on V3 (recurring features across seeds) and V5 (the same feature type recurring across models).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MLPs and transformers, across seeds and hyperparameters, implement one abstract algorithm (approximate CRT) built on approximate cosets, needing O(log n) frequencies, despite low-level differences such as clock versus pizza. They also claim universality with permutation-group coset circuits from prior work and pose a conjecture for all group tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses neuron-level sinusoidal fits, approximate cosets, and an abstract-algorithm interpretation on modular addition; it does not use the original sources' representation-alignment measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and depth affect neuron forms: deeper transformers can use second-order or superposed sinusoids, while MLPs admit the reported first-order fits. The paper also reports that hyperparameters and width affect learned frequencies and fit patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: The number of learned frequencies drops from about ⌊n/2⌋ to O(log n) when depth or trainable embeddings are added (Figs 3, 4, 41). The feature set learned therefore depends on architecture choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How many and which features networks converge to depends on architecture choices (depth, embeddings), even on one task.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS (venue given); the paper text describes the manuscript as a preprint under review.
record.problems: The evidence concerns a single synthetic task and a proposed abstraction, not pairwise representation similarity. The analysis assumes periodic or sinusoidal neuron structure and validates that assumption empirically; many plotted results are not accompanied by exact numerical fit values in the text. The study does not test whether shared data or objectives explain the common structure.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for frequency-count growth with modulus, frequency histograms, or preference for precise cosets: those results do not measure alignment between models or recurrence of the claim's specified features. Values visible only in plots and prior-work results were also excluded.

untested.parts: No comparison of alignment as model size or capability grows; no pairwise alignment metric.
Not tested: no vision-language models or paired image-caption data.
Does not quantify pairwise feature or subspace alignment between seeds (e.g. CCA, CKA, unit matching). Shared structure is shown only at the level of feature type and abstract algorithm.
Not tested: no mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
No SAE features. No direct matching of specific features or circuits across models; only the shared sinusoidal/coset form.
Not tested: no comparison of similarity metrics, metric settings or input distributions.
Not tested: no measure of alignment level or plateau, and no test of whether shared data or objectives explain the shared structure.

missing.what: Frequency histograms across 100k seeds (mod 89 and mod 91) are uniform: seeds learn different specific frequencies, while frequencies with additive relations are avoided.
All architectures prefer precise cosets (frequencies dividing 66) over approximate cosets.
Single-sine R2 fit improves as width grows (512 to 16384) in MLP, pizza and clock, over 500 models each.
Share of first-order neurons in layer 2 of a 2-layer transformer is near 100% only in a small hyperparameter region.

record.verdict_notes: Single synthetic task. The universality shown is at the level of feature type and abstract algorithm; specific features (frequencies) differ across seeds. Fit thresholds and the exact counts of failing cells are visible only in plots.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure pairwise alignment between independently trained models as model size or capability increases.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language models.
Tests for shared abstract structure across seeds, not whether individual features or shared subspaces align pairwise, or whether units/bases differ in a quantified way.
Does not map one model's representations onto another's, stitch layers, or test unpaired mappings.
Tests recurring simple-neuron and approximate-coset structure at an abstract level, not exact feature or circuit identity across models or SAE features.
Does not compare representation-similarity metrics, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not quantify incomplete or plateauing representational alignment or test whether shared data or objectives cause it.

rows.subject: MLPs and transformers (clock and pizza; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed neuron preactivations and their fit to sinusoidal functions, then interpreted their activation patterns using approximate cosets.

conditions.value: MLPs and transformers, including clock and pizza
Across the architectures, hyperparameters, seeds, moduli, and depths described in the paper

rows.measure: Whether learned neuron patterns are captured by simple sinusoidal neurons and the approximate-coset abstraction.
rows.value: The authors report that the simple-neuron assumption is empirically validated across architectures, hyperparameters, random seeds, moduli, and depth; they state that all architectures are well abstracted by approximate cosets and that layer 1 uses simple neurons.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative result as reported by the authors; it supports shared abstract structure, not measured pairwise similarity or identical features.
rows.check: Aggregate author claim spanning Figs 1–9; it mixes architectures, so for V3 only the same-architecture, across-seed part applies. Per-cell results live in R2/R3.

source_check.correct: State: partial for the aggregate V3/V5 linkage. A shared sinusoidal family and approximate-coset abstraction recur; specific frequencies vary across seeds, and deeper transformer neurons include second-order and superposed forms.
source_check.problem: The aggregate author claim is accurately reported, but observed overstates convergence of concrete features across all linked conditions.

rows.subject: MLPs (aggregate across tested depths and settings)
rows.size_stated: 1024 neurons per layer for the Figure 6 models
rows.operation_detail: Fit neuron preactivations with simple sinusoidal forms and assessed whether replacing neurons with those fits preserved model accuracy.

conditions.value: 10 different random seeds for each learning-rate and weight-decay combination in the Figure 6 experiment

rows.measure: Accuracy after replacing neurons with simple-neuron fits.
rows.baseline: The trained model's accuracy without the replacement; the comparison assumes 100% accuracy for the trained model.
rows.value: The authors report that every neuron in every layer can be fit using the stated sinusoidal form while maintaining 100% test accuracy.
rows.note: This supports the authors' abstraction across MLP layers; it is not a cross-model representation mapping test.
rows.check: The value overstates the result. Fig. 6 shows a 'large volume' of green checkmarks, not every hyperparameter cell, and a cell fails if any of its 10 seeds drops below 100%. Recording which cells fail would make this precise.

source_check.correct: State: partial across the aggregate settings. Section 4.4 reports that fitting every neuron can preserve 100% test accuracy; Figure 6 describes many successful hyperparameter cells, without asserting universal success. Each cell includes 10 seeds; one replacement result below 100% produces a failure marker when the original model achieved 100%.
source_check.problem: The value turns a possible, frequently successful replacement into an unconditional result across tested settings.

rows.subject: Transformers (clock and pizza; aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 1024 neurons per layer for the Figure 7 models
rows.operation_detail: Fit neuron preactivations by layer with first-order and, in later layers, second-order sinusoidal forms.

conditions.value: 10 different random seeds for each learning-rate and weight-decay combination in the Figure 7 experiment

rows.measure: Layer-wise form of neuron preactivations and goodness of fit to the sinusoidal abstractions.
rows.value: The authors report high R2 for first-layer fits; deeper layers can contain simple, second-order, or superposed forms. They state that fitting only first-order forms is insufficient to maintain 100% accuracy in these transformers.
rows.note: The shared approximate-coset account accommodates different layer-wise forms, but the result does not establish identical neuron-level features across models.
rows.check: Layer 1 is simple in all transformers. Later layers mix first-order, second-order and superposed forms, and Fig. 8 shows the share of first-order neurons varies strongly with hyperparameters. Partial is correct.

relationships.condition: Same-architecture MLPs and transformers across 10 seeds per hyperparameter cell and across 100k seeds
relationships.reason: Across seeds, neurons consistently learn simple sinusoids whose fits preserve accuracy, so the same feature type recurs (R1, R2, R3 layer 1).
relationships.display_finding: Neurons repeatedly learned simple sinusoids across seeds, with fits preserving accuracy in some settings, while selected frequencies varied and replacement success depended on hyperparameters.

relationships.condition: Which specific frequencies are learned across seeds, and deeper transformer layers
relationships.reason: Text, not rows: Fig. 31 shows specific frequencies spread uniformly across 100k seeds, so seeds learn different concrete features. Deeper transformer layers vary in form (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Specific frequencies were spread uniformly across 100k seeds, while deeper transformer layers varied in form.

relationships.condition: First-layer neurons in MLPs, pizza and clock transformers on modular addition
relationships.reason: Sinusoidal neurons on approximate cosets recur across all three architectures, and look identical after remapping (R1, R2, R3 layer 1).
relationships.display_finding: Neurons encoding sinusoids on approximate cosets appeared in all three architectures and looked identical after remapping.

source_check.condition: First-layer neurons in MLPs, pizza and clock transformers on modular addition
source_check.reason: R1–R3 and Figure 1 support recurring interpretable sinusoidal approximate-coset feature forms across these architectures, with qualitative equivalence after frequency normalization.

relationships.condition: Deeper layers of transformers and circuit-level mechanisms
relationships.reason: Later transformer layers contain second-order or superposed forms, unlike MLPs (R3). Clock and pizza still differ at circuit level; the shared element is an abstract template.
relationships.display_finding: Later transformer layers contained second-order or superposed forms unlike MLPs, while clock and pizza transformers retained distinct circuits despite a shared abstract template.
